newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt shares lower in quiet pre-holiday market.
newsitem.headline: Egypt shares lower in quiet pre-holiday market.

text.p: Egyptian share prices closed lower on Monday amid profit-taking in a quiet pre-holiday market.
The Capital Market Authority (CMA) all-share index closed 2.23 points lower at 284.72 on a volume of 56.89 million pounds ($16.73 million).

"It's a continuation of the profit-taking which we have been seeing for the past ten days," said Mohammed Abdullah of EFG/Hermes brokerage. "Foreign investors don't want any settlements left before the holidays.
"We'll definitely see a different market right after the holidays," he said.
About 21 million pounds of the turnover was scooped up by Housing and Development Bank in one move of 374,500 shares. The bank's shares closed down 1.50 at 56.50.
"The whole block belongs to a public sector bank. The government has asked public sector banks to offload...as part of the privatisation process," Abdullah said.
"Heliopolis shares also attracted attention," he added.
Popular realty firm Heliopolis Housing and Development was the second most active share with 10.72 million pounds changing hands. It closed down 11.25 at 430.
Some milling shares slipped or ended unchanged as they approached their dividend payment period.

East Delta Flour Mills closed 0.91 down at 52.99, Central and West Delta Flour Mills was unchanged at 81.50, but Upper Egypt Flour Mills closed 1.83 lower at 64.33 while North Cairo Flour Mills rose 1.18 to 132.55.
The CMAindex for openly traded firms fell to 427.40 from 429.04 on Sunday while the index for rarely traded "closed" firms fell to 200.45 from 202.49.
Of the 85 shares traded, 17 rose, 31 fell and 37 ended the day unchanged, the CMA said.
